problems.problem: The previous version's two arcs are gone (verified: no dark concave ceiling rim at the top, no convex hill crest behind the base), but the regenerated sweep still shows one readable straight horizon: a horizontal tonal edge crossing the full canvas at y≈960-970, exactly level with the product base (base_y 979) and clearly visible in the contact crop as a straight boundary behind both contact shadows. The declared 'Porcelain Sweep' concept requires one continuous invisible curve; this edge reads as a wall/floor seam line running through the silhouette's contact zone instead of a quiet seamless plane.

Because the visible seam sits at the same height as the contact line, the eye reads two stacked grounds: the product appears to stand on the seam rather than in front of a continuous floor. Below the label band (rule y≈1046, title ink 1100-1184) roughly 256px of empty foreground remains to the canvas bottom; references 3 and 5 anchor their lower zones with a tonal block or pedestal edge, so the bottom fifth here still reads as unresolved dead space rather than intentional negative space.

The gallery-label band is internally aligned (rule center ≈568 vs title optical center ≈557, tracking consistent) but sits in the brightest zone of the frame directly under the seam, so the 240px hairline rule nearly vanishes against the pale floor and the word lacks the tonal separation the reference type blocks enjoy; hierarchy is competent yet under-weighted for a luxury campaign.

References 3-5 each commit to one unmistakable spatial idea (graded violet field, macro diagonal on warm gradient, pedestal against sky). This poster's idea (seamless paper sweep, low letter-spaced label) is now close, but the residual horizon seam and the thin label band keep it one step below reference polish: the set still reads as 'backdrop plus pasted cutout with a shadow' rather than a single photographed environment.
